A task is assigned early in the meeting and later in the same meeting is either reassigned to someone else (status reassigned, owner = new owner, previous_owners lists the original) or dropped entirely (status dropped).

argv:
You generate synthetic meeting transcripts with gold annotations for LiveMinutes, a research dataset modeled on the AMI Meeting Corpus scenario meetings.

In AMI scenario meetings, a team of four plays a design team in a fictional company. The roles are Project Manager (PM), Marketing Expert (ME), User Interface designer (UI) and Industrial Designer (ID). A series has four meetings: (a) kickoff, (b) functional design, (c) conceptual design, (d) detailed design. Later meetings refer back to earlier ones.

Write natural spoken conversation the way AMI transcripts read: short turns, fillers ("um", "uh", "yeah"), backchannels ("mm-hmm", "okay"), interruptions, people building on each other, and some disfluency. Do not write a screenplay. Do not narrate. No stage directions.

Each segment is one dialogue-act-like unit: one speaker, usually one clause or short sentence, sometimes just a backchannel. Give each segment an AMI dialogue-act type from this set:
  bck backchannel, stl stall, fra fragment, inf inform, sug suggest, ass assess,
  el.inf elicit-inform, el.sug elicit-offer-or-suggestion, el.ass elicit-assessment,
  el.und elicit-comment-understanding, off offer, und comment-about-understanding,
  be.pos be-positive, be.neg be-negative, oth other

Absent participants NEVER speak. Speaker labels are ground truth: use only the labels you are given.

The gold annotations must be exactly true of the transcript you write. Refer to segments by their "n" number. Every number you cite must exist.

Output a single JSON object and nothing else: no prose, no markdown fences.

request.user:
Write meeting SY0208c: meeting "c" (conceptual design) of series SY0208.

PROJECT
The team is designing a library self-checkout kiosk.

PARTICIPANTS (label, role, status for this meeting)
A  Project Manager (PM)  Priya  present
B  Industrial Designer (ID)  Tomasz  present
C  Marketing Expert (ME)  Helen  present
D  User Interface designer (UI)  Marcus  ABSENT, never speaks

EARLIER MEETINGS IN THIS SERIES
Stay consistent with them. Refer back to them, follow up on their open action items, and keep the same product and team.

[SY0208a, kickoff]
  abstract: The project manager opened the kickoff meeting, noted that the industrial designer was absent through illness, and had the marketing expert and user interface designer introduce themselves. She presented the project: a self-checkout kiosk sold to public library authorities, with a production cost target of under 3,500 euros per unit including screen, scanner, receipt printer and casing. The team agreed that a single kiosk should handle both borrowing and returns, and discussed whether the kiosk should read RFID tags, barcodes or both, which was handed to the absent industrial designer along with the question of whether a receipt printer is needed. The marketing expert described a very broad user group, especially older borrowers, children and non-native speakers, which led to calls for a simple interface with big buttons and language selection by language name. A card-free face recognition idea from the user interface designer was parked over privacy concerns, and the task of obtaining library usage data moved from the marketing expert to the user interface designer.
  decisions: The kiosk will handle both borrowing and returns on one unit. Language selection will use language names rather than flags. The whiteboard tool exercise was skipped because a team member was absent.
  actions: The industrial designer (absent) will compare RFID pads and barcode scanners and check whether supporting both fits the budget. The industrial designer (absent) will check whether a receipt printer is needed. The user interface designer will obtain checkout usage numbers and peak times from the library; this task was originally given to the marketing expert. The marketing expert will research existing self-checkout kiosks on the market, their costs and common complaints. The user interface designer will draft a rough user flow (card, books, confirm, receipt). The project manager will email the industrial designer about his tasks and send the minutes to everyone.
  problems: It is unresolved whether the kiosk must support both RFID and barcodes and whether that fits the 3,500 euro cost target. It is unclear whether a receipt printer is needed. Face recognition sign-in was parked due to library privacy concerns. The user base is very broad, so the interface must work for older borrowers, children and non-native speakers.
  action item SY0208a.ai1: Research RFID pads versus barcode scanners and whether supporting both fits the budget (owner B, active)
  action item SY0208a.ai2: Check whether the kiosk needs a receipt printer (owner B, active)
  action item SY0208a.ai3: Obtain library usage numbers: checkouts per day and peak times (circulation data) (owner D, reassigned)
  action item SY0208a.ai4: Research existing self-checkout kiosks on the market, their costs and common complaints (owner C, active)
  action item SY0208a.ai5: Draft a rough user flow (card, books, confirm, receipt) (owner D, active)
  action item SY0208a.ai6: Email the industrial designer about his assigned tasks (owner A, active)
  action item SY0208a.ai7: Send meeting minutes to everyone today (owner A, active)
  fact (absence): Tomasz, the industrial designer, was absent because he was off sick.
  fact (unagreed_proposal): The user interface designer suggested the kiosk might need to support both RFID and barcodes; this was not decided and was passed to the industrial designer.
  fact (unagreed_proposal): The user interface designer proposed card-free face recognition sign-in; it was parked over privacy concerns.
  fact (unagreed_proposal): The user interface designer suggested using flags for language selection; this was rejected.
  fact (plan_change): Obtaining library usage numbers was first given to Helen (marketing expert) and then reassigned to Marcus (user interface designer).
  fact (action_item_removed): Helen was taken off the usage-numbers task because of her market research workload.

[SY0208b, functional design]
  abstract: The project manager welcomed back the industrial designer, recapped the kickoff decisions and confirmed that he had received her email about his tasks. The marketing expert reported that existing self-checkout kiosks cost between 9,000 and 20,000 euros per unit, and that users most often complain about missed items in stacks, confusing error messages and security tags that are not deactivated. She also reported that users want a running list of their borrowed items on screen. The industrial designer presented component costs: about 600 euros for an RFID pad, 150 euros for a barcode scanner, 700 for the touchscreen, 500 for the PC, 800 for the casing and 200 for a thermal printer, about 2,950 euros in total. The team agreed to support both RFID and barcodes and to keep the printer. The user interface designer reported about 1,200 checkouts a day at the main branch, with peaks on Saturday mornings and weekdays from three to six. He set a target of under one minute per borrow and presented a flow that starts with a borrow/return screen with language names. Voice instructions were proposed and parked, and the question of connecting to the library catalogue system was raised but not assigned to anyone.
  decisions: The kiosk will read both RFID tags and barcodes. A small thermal receipt printer will be included instead of email-only receipts. The start screen will have two large buttons, borrow and return, with language names along the bottom.
  actions: The industrial designer will look into how the kiosk deactivates security tags for RFID and barcode items. The marketing expert offered first, but he took it because it is tied to the reader. The industrial designer will firm up the component costing and start on the casing. The user interface designer will turn the user flow into rough screen sketches for borrowing and returns. The marketing expert will research accessibility guidelines, such as screen height for wheelchair users and children. The project manager will send the minutes out tonight. Checking which catalogue systems libraries run and whether there is a standard connection was raised, but nobody took it.
  problems: Integration with the libraries' catalogue systems is unresolved and has no owner. Casing costs could rise and eat into the roughly 550 euro margin under the 3,500 euro target. Security tag deactivation must be solved to avoid gate alarms, a common complaint about existing kiosks. Borrowing must be fast, under a minute, to handle after-school and Saturday peaks. Voice instructions were parked over noise concerns in a quiet library.
  action item SY0208b.ai1: Look into security tag deactivation for RFID and barcode items so gate alarms are not triggered (owner B, active)
  action item SY0208b.ai2: Check which catalogue systems the libraries run and whether there is a standard connection for the kiosk to record loans (owner no owner, active)
  action item SY0208b.ai3: Firm up the component costing and start on the casing design (owner B, active)
  action item SY0208b.ai4: Turn the user flow into rough screen sketches for borrowing and returns (owner D, active)
  action item SY0208b.ai5: Research accessibility guidelines such as screen height for wheelchair users and children (owner C, active)
  action item SY0208b.ai6: Send the meeting minutes out tonight (owner A, active)
  fact (unagreed_proposal): The marketing expert suggested emailing receipts instead of printing them; the team kept the printer because not all borrowers, especially children, have email.
  fact (unagreed_proposal): The user interface designer suggested voice instructions that read the steps out loud; it was parked over noise concerns in the library.

EDGE CASES THIS MEETING MUST CONTAIN
Weave each one naturally into the project discussion. Each must be clearly present, and each must be tagged with the segments where it happens.
- F2_TASK_TO_ABSENT [F2]: A task is assigned to a team member who is absent from this meeting. The gold action item owner is that absent participant.
  Required gold labels: action_items, edge_cases.
- F2_REASSIGNED_OR_DROPPED [F2]: A task is assigned early in the meeting and later in the same meeting is either reassigned to someone else (status reassigned, owner = new owner, previous_owners lists the original) or dropped entirely (status dropped).
  Required gold labels: action_items, edge_cases.

LENGTH
Between 90 and 140 segments.

GOLD LABELS
- summary: AMI-style abstractive summary in third person, using role names ("The project manager ..."). Sections: abstract (3-6 sentences), actions, decisions, problems (open issues). It reflects the meeting's FINAL state: corrected values, final plans, and no jokes or tangents reported as content.
- action_items: every task arising in the meeting. owner is the speaker label of the FINAL owner, and may be an absent participant. owner is null ONLY for a task nobody takes, with owner_unclear true. status is the final status: active, reassigned (owner changed; previous_owners lists earlier owners) or dropped. history lists the events in order. evidence_segments lists the supporting segments.
- qa_facts: atomic facts someone could later ask about ("Who was asked to ...?", "Did the team agree on ...?"). Include every decision (agreed true), every proposal nobody agreed to (type unagreed_proposal, agreed false), action items, removed action items, absences, and plan changes. Because this meeting follows earlier ones, include at least one fact of type reference_to_prior_meeting, with refers_to_meeting set, at a point where someone refers back to an earlier meeting. Do NOT write questions.
- edge_cases: one entry per edge case above, with its scenario_id and the segment numbers that contain it.

OUTPUT JSON SHAPE
{
  "segments": [{"n": 1, "speaker": "A", "da_type": "inf", "text": "..."}],
  "summary": {"abstract": ["..."], "actions": ["..."], "decisions": ["..."], "problems": ["..."]},
  "action_items": [{"n": 1, "description": "...", "owner": "C", "owner_unclear": false, "status": "active", "previous_owners": [], "history": [{"segment": 12, "event": "assigned", "by": "A", "owner": "C"}], "evidence_segments": [12, 13]}],
  "qa_facts": [{"type": "decision", "fact": "...", "agreed": true, "related_action_item": null, "refers_to_meeting": null, "evidence_segments": [40]}],
  "edge_cases": [{"scenario_id": "...", "segments": [20, 21, 22], "note": "one line on how it appears"}]
}
history events: proposed, offered, assigned, accepted, reassigned, dropped, restated. qa_facts types: decision, unagreed_proposal, action_item, action_item_removed, absence, plan_change, reference_to_prior_meeting, other. related_action_item is an action item's "n" or null. refers_to_meeting is an earlier meeting ID of this series or null.
